question.problem:
Which of the following vector fields have a stream function?

I. $F(x,y)=3x\,i-{y}^{2}\,j$

II. $F(x,y)=x\,i+x{y}^{2}\,j$

III. $F(x,y)={x}^{2}\,i-2xy\,j$
question.worked_solution:
A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each vector field.

- Vector field I doesn't have a stream function. The partial derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=3,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=3+(-2y)\ne 0.
$$

- Vector field II doesn't have a stream function. The partial derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =2xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=1+2xy\ne 0.
$$

- Vector field III has a stream function. Indeed, the partial derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=2x+(-2x)=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
